marks.gloss_en: if wine came to them during the meal, each and every one blesses for himself
היו יושבין כל אחד ואחד כו׳ -- from the mishnah's wording 'if they reclined': reclining, yes; not reclining, no
ורמינהו: עשרה שהיו הולכים בדרך... ישבו לאכול... אחד מברך לכולם -- קתני ישבו אף על פי שלא הסבו: the baraita has sitting suffice without reclining
if they reclined -- yes [one blesses for all]; if they did not recline -- no
(next piska) כגון דאמרי נזיל וניכול לחמא בדוך פלן -- [the baraita speaks of] a case where they said 'let us go and eat bread in such-and-such a place'
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: [the baraita speaks of a case] where they said 'let us go and eat bread in such-and-such a place'
reading 1: Beit Shammai dispute the first clause -- for the tanna kama bread exempts appetizers and all the more so a cooked dish; Beit Shammai say bread does not exempt even a cooked dish
אמר ליה: יישר, וכן אמר רבי יהושע בן לוי -- well done; RYBL said so too (on the rest of the year one blesses over each cup)
on a weekday Rava blessed [over wine] before the meal and blessed again after the meal
לא סבר לה מר להא דרבי יהושע בן לוי?! -- on a festival, by RYBL, the first blessing suffices; why does the master bless over each cup?
on a festival Abaye blessed over each and every cup

איתיביה רבא לרב נחמן: wine during the meal -- each blesses for himself; after the meal -- one blesses for all: the after-meal wine gets a blessing although wine came during the meal, so the during-meal wine did not exempt it
הכי קאמר: if wine came to them not during the meal but only after it, one blesses for all (= p_rn_hachi_kaamar)
Rav Nachman: this is what the mishnah says -- if wine came to them not during the meal but only after it, one blesses for all
R' Yochanan: [the mishnah's rule] was taught only of Shabbatot and festivals
RYBL: [the mishnah's rule] was taught only of Shabbatot and festivals, when a man comes out of the bathhouse, and at bloodletting
wine that came during the meal: its blessing exempts the wine after the meal
